messages.author: Zhuoran Long
messages.body:
Hi,
I‘m trying to use the H-REMD for umbrella sampling. I'm using a generalized
distance reaction coordinate, which is not periodic. Therefore I tried the
gremd_acyc keyword. However, it gives the "error in reading namelist cntrl"
using sander.MPI and amber version 20.11. This error disappears when not
including this keyword. I also tried version 20.06 and 22.00 but neither
version works. I need to use the semiempirical QM/MM so I can't switch to
pmemd.MPI.
I notice that this keyword is introduced in Sept 2019. I can't find any
examples including the amber test codes.
I paste my input file below. Any suggestions or examples are appreciated.
Best,
Zhuoran
HREMD-Umbrella sampling
&cntrl
imin = 0,
irest = 1,
iwrap = 1,
ntx = 5,
ntxo= 1,
nstlim= 100,
dt = 0.001,
ntc = 1,
ntf = 1,
cut = 8,
ntb = 2,
ntp = 1,
pres0 = 1.0,
taup= 5.0,
ntpr= 500,
ntwx= 500,
ntt = 3,
gamma_ln = 1.0,
temp0 = 300.0,
ioutfm= 1,
ifqnt = 1,
nmropt= 1,
ig = 4746,
numexchg = 5,
gremd_acyc=1
/
&qmmm
qmmask=':1',
qmcharge=-2,
qm_theory='PM3',
qmshake=1,
qm_ewald=1, qm_pme=1,
/
&wt
type='DUMPFREQ', istep1=500,
/
&wt
type='END',
/
DISANG=disang_cocc_001.in
DUMPAVE=cocc_001.dat

messages.author: Adrian Roitberg
messages.body:
Hi
As far as I know, that keyword has nothing to do with periodicity. It is
there to enable an odd number of replicas, instead of the usual even_number
So, try to use an even number of replicas without gremd_acyc=1 and see
what happens.
adrian

messages.author: Zhuoran Long
messages.body:
Hi Adrian,
The md can run after removing the gremd_acyc keyword. However it involving
exchange between the first and last replicas. In my case, the
generalized distance reaction coordinates are restrained to about -2
Angstrom and +2 Angstrom in these two replicas.
The amber 2021 manual says, " gremd_acyc (H-REMD only) When set to 1, the
exchange between the first and the last replicas will not be considered and
odd numbers of replicas are allowed. Default: 0". That's why I want to use
this keyword.
Thank you,
Zhuoran

messages.author: Adrian Roitberg
messages.body:
Yes, you are right, that is what that keyword is supposed to do.
However, if you do not use it, the only thing that happens is that the
remd will try to exchange the first and last replicas, as you mentioned.
If they are too far apart, they will "never" exchange, which is the
correct behavior.
Bottom-line, there is nothing to gain from using it if you have an even
number of replicas.
adrian

messages.author: Brian Radak
messages.body:
Actually (though this may be outdated advice), one might still want to use
the keyword in certain cases when using the GPU code and you know exchanges
should never occur.
At one point we observed that large energy differences in the GTI
alchemical code were tricking the PRNG routines into incorrectly accepting
exchanges when they definitely should not have been. It seemed to be a
mixture of overflow in the energy code and odd behavior in the PRNG (which
produces overly regular values in exchange for reproducible behavior across
GPU architectures).
Maybe this was fixed...
BKR

messages.author: accuratefreeenergy–––
messages.body:
Hi Adrian and Zhuoran,
As the implementer of this keyword, my answer:
1. If you have odd-number of replicas, you can NOT do exchange between the first and the last, or you will leave one middle replica alone without doing exchange.
2. Although the exchange between the first and the last replicas seems not a big deal--theoretically, sometimes it will give troubles in TI calculations: you need to evaluate the potential energy based on the Hamiltonian of the first replica with the conformation of the last replica--such calculations could lead GPU overflows and crash the simulation. In fact, this was the main reason I implemented this keyword to prevent the exchange between the first and the last.
Taisung
-----Original Message-----
From: Adrian Roitberg via AMBER <amber.ambermd.org>
Sent: Tuesday, August 16, 2022 11:44 AM
To: Zhuoran Long <zl1277.nyu.
edu>; AMBER Mailing List <amber.ambermd.
org>
Subject: Re: [AMBER] gremd_acyc keyword for H-REMD
Yes, you are right, that is what that keyword is supposed to do.
However, if you do not use it, the only thing that happens is that the remd will try to exchange the first and last replicas, as you mentioned.
If they are too far apart, they will "never" exchange, which is the correct behavior.
Bottom-line, there is nothing to gain from using it if you have an even number of replicas.
adrian
